stocks.note: Numbers as of market close on May 14th.
stocks.news: All three indices closed strong on Thursday with the S&P crossing 7,500 and DOW back over 50K. The headline story: Cerebras (CBRS +68.15%) just pulled off the biggest U.S. tech IPO since Uber, raising $5.55B and opening at $350 on Nasdaq, valuing the AI chipmaker above $100B. One twist worth flagging: a single UAE university accounted for 62% of Cerebras's revenue last year, so the concentration risk is real. Investors are reading this as the start of the AI IPO floodgates, SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic are next in line. Ford (F +6.71%) had its best back-to-back trading days since 2020, with Morgan Stanley flagging the company's new battery storage unit as potentially worth $10B if they ink deals with the AI data center hyperscalers. Trump in China delivered three signals: Xi promised business doors will "open wider," China agreed to buy 200 planes from Boeing (BA -4.73% on tariff-related noise anyway), and Beijing warned the U.S. not to interfere with Taiwan. TSMC (TSM +4.48%) now holds a bigger share of MSCI Emerging Markets than India does as a whole country. That's how concentrated the AI thesis has gotten.

economy.note: US 10-Year and Gold as of 4:00 PM ET May 14th; WTI Crude reflects today's intraday move via investing.com.
economy.commentary:
The 10-year stepped up to 4.49% as the bond market reprices around persistent inflation, gold cooled to $4,658, and WTI ripped another +4.46% to $105.68. Brent essentially matched at $105.72, meaning the spread has collapsed and both grades are now trading together. The Iran-war energy premium continues to feed everything.

The defining macro signal of the week: CME now puts Fed rate-cut odds for 2026 at just 1.6%. A week ago that figure was still in the teens. With PPI at 6%, CPI at 3.8%, and Warsh installed as the new hawkish Fed Chair, the rate-cut path that anchored 2025's bull market has been priced out. Treasury Secretary Bessent is publicly forecasting "substantial disinflation in a few months," but the bond market is voting with its feet in the opposite direction.

Retirement geography flag for clients thinking about exit-state planning: a comfortable retirement in Hawaii now costs $156,610 a year while West Virginia comes in at $33,223, a $123K gap on the same Social Security check. That's a useful number to have in conversations with downsizing clients who are weighing Bay Area exit options.

real_estate.homebuilder: Rates Pop Another +10 BPs To 6.62% (+20 BPs Weekly); CME Fed-Cut Odds For 2026 Now 1.6%; Friday Listing Surge
real_estate.commentary:
Three threads to close the week with clients.

First, the rate march continued today. The 30-year jumped another 10 bps to 6.62%, the 15-year is at 6.09%. That's +20 bps from Monday's 6.42% in a single week, the largest weekly rate movement we have tracked this year. MND today is flagging "MBS prices significantly weaker" which means the move likely continues into Friday's close. The Wednesday MBA Mortgage Applications survey shows applications stayed flat week-over-week, meaning buyers absorbed the rate jump and kept going. That's the data point worth reading aloud to any fence-sitting client. The market is not waiting for the Fed.

Second, the "rates fall in 2026" thesis is mathematically dead now. CME puts Fed rate-cut odds for 2026 at 1.6%, down from the teens a week ago. Treasury Secretary Bessent is the only major voice still calling for disinflation. Any client telling you they are waiting for cuts is making a bet against a 98.4% probability. Frame the conversation that way and the urgency reframes itself.

Third, a headline anecdote worth bookmarking: a $3M Nantucket house is being given away for free on the condition the buyer relocates it within 180 days (moving cost $150K to $500K). Empty Nantucket lots start at $1.65M, so it's still arguably a deal. The land-vs-structure economics on the coasts have completely inverted in some markets, and the Bay Area's land scarcity is the same dynamic running in reverse. Worth using as a conversation opener with luxury clients.

For listing agents: the week's data tells your story for you. Rates +20 bps in 5 days. Fed cuts at 1.6% odds. CPI 3.8%, PPI 6%. Send a written touchpoint to every active prospect this weekend with those numbers in the body. The buyers who close in May are the buyers who don't wait for June.

For buyer agents: with 250 new listings on the board today and inventory at 2,967, the selection is genuinely improving. Active buyers gained leverage today on tour-day decisions. Frame the math for them: rates are not getting better in their timeframe, and supply is finally moving.
